incident: Irish Health Service Executive (HSE) — Conti ransomware (Wizard Spider), 14 May 2021

sources.title: PwC, Conti cyber attack on the HSE — Independent Post Incident Review (full report, Dec 2021)
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (16/18 March phishing Excel on Patient Zero workstation), 23 March persistence, 31 March AV in monitor mode, 7 May first HSE server compromise + AD recon + highly privileged accounts, 8-12 May six voluntary + one statutory hospital compromised, 10 May Hospital C DC alert, 12 May Hospital A alert, 13 May AV vendor email (16 systems), 14 May 01:00 execution / 02:50 reports / 04:36 encryption identified in data centre, services lost (NIMIS, labs, radiotherapy, MN-CMS, iPMS), 80% encrypted, 1,075/1,087 apps recovered by 21 Sep

sources.title: KrebsOnSecurity, Inside Ireland's Public Healthcare Ransomware Scare (13 Dec 2021, summarising PwC)
sources.what_it_gave: 31 March Cobalt Strike + Mimikatz detected on Patient Zero but not blocked; 7 May attacker compromised HSE servers; 10 May Hospital C AV detected Cobalt Strike on two systems, evidence at Hospital C and Hospital L; 13 May vendor email 'at least 16 systems' since 7 May; $20m demand; 30,000+ Windows 7 workstations

sources.title: HHS HC3, Lessons learned from the HSE cyber attack (summary of PwC review)
sources.what_it_gave: 7 May antivirus flagged Cobalt Strike on six servers, 'alerts were not appropriately actioned'; two voluntary hospitals saw suspicious activity before execution; ~80% of environment encrypted; ~700 GB exfiltrated; Exchange encrypted; National Healthcare Network disconnected

sources.title: The Register, Irish health service's Conti ransomware report (10 Dec 2021)
sources.what_it_gave: Hospital A reset 4,500 passwords after activating IR plan; 'exploited an unpatched known vulnerability' to reach a hospital AD domain; HSE wrongly concluded activity originated from Hospital A

sources.title: Irish Times, Cyberattack: HSE faces final bill of at least €100m (27 May 2021, HSE CEO briefing)
sources.what_it_gave: HSE statements on impact: ~80,000 devices, NIMIS at 24 of 64 sites, 16 of 44 labs offline, ~7,000 appointments/day cancelled, cost >= EUR 100m

narrative_before: On 16 March 2021 a phishing email with a malicious Excel attachment was sent to an HSE user; it was opened on 18 March on the 'Patient Zero Workstation' and the attacker achieved persistence by 23 March (PwC pp. 2, 28). On 31 March the HSE antivirus detected Cobalt Strike and Mimikatz on that workstation but 'was set to monitor mode so it did not block the malicious commands' and no incident was raised (PwC p. 29). On 7 May the attacker 'conducted AD and domain reconnaissance, and compromised further systems within the HSE' and 'was identified as using highly privileged accounts for the first time'; antivirus flagged Cobalt Strike on six HSE servers that day and the alerts were not actioned (PwC p. 29; HHS). Between 8 and 12 May six voluntary hospitals and one statutory hospital were compromised; Hospital C found malicious activity on a domain controller on 10 May, Hospital A alerted the HSE on 12 May and reset 4,500 passwords, and on 13 May the AV vendor emailed about 'unhandled threat events since 7 May 2021 on at least 16 systems' — the HSE response was to ask the server team to restart servers (PwC pp. 28-30). At 01:00 on 14 May Conti was executed; hospitals reported encrypted systems at 02:50, encryption in the HSE data centre was identified at 04:36, and the HSE shut down all IT and the National Healthcare Network. About 80% of the environment was encrypted and ~700 GB exfiltrated; NIMIS radiology, laboratory, radiotherapy, maternity (MN-CMS) and iPMS systems were lost, ~7,000 appointments a day were cancelled, a decryption key appeared on 20 May, full server decryption took until September 2021 and the HSE put the cost at >= EUR 100m (PwC pp. 15, 32-33; HHS; Irish Times).

detection_moments.description: 31 March 2021: HSE antivirus detects Cobalt Strike and Mimikatz on the Patient Zero workstation; AV in monitor mode, nothing blocked, no incident opened. Mimikatz = credential dumping (T1003) -> 8.
detection_moments.evidence: 'The antivirus software was set to monitor mode so it did not block the malicious commands' (PwC p. 29); 'HSE antivirus detects Cobalt Strike and Mimikatz on the patient zero workstation, but the software is in monitor mode' (KrebsOnSecurity summary).

detection_moments.description: 7 May 2021: attacker performs AD/domain reconnaissance, uses highly privileged accounts for the first time and compromises HSE servers; antivirus flags Cobalt Strike on six servers but alerts are not actioned.
detection_moments.evidence: 'conducted AD and domain reconnaissance, and compromised further systems within the HSE ... using highly privileged accounts for the first time' (PwC p. 29); 'Antivirus flagged Cobalt Strike on six servers ... these alerts were not appropriately actioned' (HHS HC3 summary of PwC).

detection_moments.description: 10 May 2021: Hospital C identifies malicious activity on a domain controller and its AV detects Cobalt Strike on two systems but fails to quarantine; Hospital C's provider rates it low risk, no IR investigation; evidence of compromise also at Hospital L.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Hospital C identified malicious activity on a domain controller' (PwC p. 28); 'Hospital C's antivirus software detected Cobalt Strike on two systems but failed to quarantine the malicious files' and 'did not initiate a cyber incident response investigation' (PwC p. 29); 'Auditors first find evidence of compromise at Hospital C and Hospital L' (KrebsOnSecurity).

detection_moments.description: 12-13 May 2021: Hospital A alerts the HSE OoCIO and resets 4,500 passwords; attacker browses folders and opens files on HSE systems; AV vendor emails HSE Security Operations about unhandled threat events on at least 16 systems since 7 May; HSE asks server team to restart servers and wrongly attributes activity to Hospital A. Last chance before detonation.
detection_moments.evidence: 'outlined that there were unhandled threat events since 7 May 2021 on at least 16 systems' and 'requested that the Server team restart servers' (PwC p. 30); 'The Attacker browsed folders and opened files on HSE systems from 12 to 13 May' (PwC p. 28); 'They reset passwords for 4,500' (PwC p. 29); 'incorrectly concluded in an email between the HSE teams that the suspicious activity originated from Hospital A' (PwC p. 30).

detection_moments.description: 14 May 2021 01:00-04:41: Conti executed in the HSE, Hospital C and Hospital K; hospitals report encrypted systems at 02:50; HSE identifies malicious encryption on multiple data-centre servers at 04:36 and invokes the Critical Incident Process at 04:41. This is the moment of actual incident declaration (T1486 = 9). Hospital A and Hospital L are excluded because Hospital A blocked execution and the report does not say Hospital L was encrypted.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the Attacker executed ransomware on systems within the HSE, Hospital C, Hospital K' (PwC p. 30); 02:50 service desk reports of 'multiple systems being unavailable'; 04:36 'identified malicious encryption on multiple servers in the HSE's data centre'; 04:41 'the HSE invoked their Critical Incident Process' (PwC pp. 30-31).

attack_path: Phishing email (16 Mar) with malicious Excel attachment opened 18 Mar; persistence 23 Mar — T1566.001, T1204.002
Cobalt Strike + Mimikatz credential dumping (31 Mar), AD and domain reconnaissance and use of highly privileged accounts (7 May) — T1003, T1087, T1078.002
First HSE server compromise 7 May, Cobalt Strike beacon flagged by AV — T1021, T1071
Further HSE servers compromised with privileged domain accounts, Cobalt Strike on six servers 7 May — T1078.002, T1021
Spread over the National Healthcare Network to voluntary hospitals 8-12 May; Hospital C Cobalt Strike on two systems — T1021
Malicious activity on Hospital C domain controller 10 May; 'likely exploited an unpatched known vulnerability' to access a hospital AD domain 11 May — T1210, T1003
Hospital A compromised then blocked after it detected activity 12 May and reset 4,500 passwords — T1021
Attacker browsed folders and opened files on HSE systems 12-13 May; ~700 GB exfiltrated — T1083, T1005, T1048
Conti executed 01:00 14 May across HSE data centre servers (NIMIS, labs, iPMS, MN-CMS, radiotherapy, Exchange), Hospital C and Hospital K — T1486
ambiguities: The public PwC report does not name the six HSE servers flagged on 7 May nor the '16 systems' of 13 May; srv_hse_1..6 are generic placeholders (rule 1, generic group 3-10).

The report does not state which host the attacker pivoted from to reach each HSE server or hospital; links dc -> srv_* and dc -> hospitals are modelled from the statement that the attacker used highly privileged domain accounts to 'compromise further systems' (p. 29). The exact pivot sequence is not public.
Hospital letters (A, C, K, L) are PwC anonymisations; real hospital names are redacted. Whether Hospital L was encrypted is not stated, so it is left out of m5.

Hospital A is described as having detected and blocked the attack; whether its systems were fully compromised before blocking is not stated, so srv_hosp_a is given lateral-tool risk 6 rather than 8/9.
Appendix E (detailed technical timeline) could not be retrieved in this session (PDF text truncated); the 31 March and 7 May details come from pp. 28-30 and from Krebs/HHS summaries of the report.
depends_on left empty for data-centre services: the report does not state that NIMIS/LIS/iPMS depend on AD, though it is likely.

Radiotherapy/maternity/radiology are clinically significant but the report does not say their loss directly endangered life, so disruption 4 and value 25 (not 5/30) and isolatable=true (no medical devices named).
Exfiltration volume ~700 GB comes from the HHS HC3 summary, not the PwC text retrieved; ransom demand $20m from Krebs.
Workstation count >30,000 (Krebs) reduced to 3 generic pc_hse_* plus Patient Zero to stay within ~25 machines.
Exchange email encrypted per HHS summary; the PwC pages retrieved mention loss of email but not the server name.
